Rashi on Pesachim 60b:10:1.hebrew: דתנן נמנין עליו ומושכין ידיהן ממנו עד שישחט - הבא למנות עליו ימנה, והרוצה למשוך ידיו ממנו שכבר נמנה עליו מושך. הלכך, לא אלים סתמא דלאוכליו; ואף על גב דאתיא מחשבת שלא לאוכליו ומפקא ליה מסתמא ופסל ליה, שאני לן היכא דאמר "לאוכליו" ברישא מהיכא דלא אמר, דהתם טעמא משום דלא אלים סתמיה הוא, ואיכא למימר אימשכו להו קמאי ואימנו עליה חולה וזקן ואישתחיט כוליה שלא לאוכליו. וכי אמר "לאוכליו ושלא לאוכליו", הוו להו מקצת אוכלין ולא פסלי:
Rashi on Pesachim 60b:10:1.english: For we learned [in a Mishnah]: People may register for it and withdraw their hands from it until it is slaughtered - Whoever comes to register for it may register, and whoever wishes to withdraw his hands from it, having already registered for it, may withdraw. Therefore, its unspecified [status] as being for those who can eat it is not strong; and even though an intention for those who cannot eat it comes and removes it from its unspecified [status] and disqualifies it, there is a difference between where he said "for those who can eat it" first and where he did not say [it], for there [where he did not say it] the reason is because its unspecified [status] is not strong, and one can say that the first [registrants] withdrew and a sick person and an elderly person registered for it, so the entire [offering] was slaughtered for those who cannot eat it. Whereas when he says "for those who can eat it and for those who cannot eat it," there are some who can eat it, and [those who cannot] do not disqualify [it].

Rashi on Pesachim 60b:11:1.hebrew: ה"ג פסח ששחטו בשאר ימות השנה בשינוי בעלים מהו - ול"ג לשמו. שחטו סתם בשינוי בעלים — של ראובן היה ושחטו לשם שמעון, אבל לא עקר שם פסח ממנו:
Rashi on Pesachim 60b:11:1.english: This is how we read [the text]: "A Paschal lamb that one slaughtered on the rest of the days of the year with a change of owner, what is [its status]?" - And we do not read "for its own sake." [Rather,] he slaughtered it unspecifically with a change of owner — [that is,] it belonged to Reuven and he slaughtered it for the sake of Shimon, but he did not uproot the designation of Paschal lamb from it.

Rashi on Pesachim 60b:11:2.english: Like a change of sanctity - Not for its own sake.

Rashi on Pesachim 60b:12:1.hebrew: שינוי בעלים פוסל - בפסח בזמנו לגמרי, וכן בחטאת. ובשאר זבחים מונען מלעלות לשם חובה, וכל תורת שינוי קודש עליהן, בשמעתא קמייתא דזבחים:
Rashi on Pesachim 60b:12:1.english: A change in owner invalidates - [It invalidates] a Paschal offering in its proper time completely, and likewise a sin-offering. And with other offerings, it prevents them from counting toward [the owner's] obligation, and the entire law of a change in sanctity [applies] to them, [as taught] in the first sugya of Zevachim.

Rashi on Pesachim 60b:13:1.english: Its disqualification is in its body - For his intention is regarding the offering itself.

Rashi on Pesachim 60b:13:2.hebrew: וישנו בארבע עבודות - שחט או קיבל דמו (או זרק או הלך) שלא לשמו, פסול, דבכל ארבע עבודות דם ילפינן ליה לפוסלה בפ"ק דזבחים (ד' ז.): שחיטה — מזבח פסח, שתהא זביחתו לשם פסח, ושאר עבודות — מועשית פסח, שיהו כל עשיותיו לשם פסח:
Rashi on Pesachim 60b:13:2.english: And it applies to four rites - [If] one slaughtered [it] or received its blood (or sprinkled [it] or conveyed [it]) not for its own sake, [it is] disqualified, for we derive it with respect to all four blood rites to disqualify it in the first chapter of Zevachim (7a): slaughter [is derived] from "sacrifice of a Passover-offering," [meaning] that its slaughtering must be for the sake of a Passover-offering, and the other rites from "and you shall perform a Passover-offering," [meaning] that all of its performances must be for the sake of a Passover-offering.

Rashi on Pesachim 60b:1:1.hebrew: אלא לאו בעבודה אחת - אף בעבודה אחת כשר, ומתני' בין בעבודה אחת בין בשתי עבודות קאמר. בעבודה אחת, כגון בשחיטה, מכשר ליה, דמשום מקצת אוכלין לא פסלי. ובשתי עבודות, כגון שחט לאוכליו וזרק שלא לאוכליו, אף על גב דכולה זריקה שלא לאוכליו — כשר, משום דאין מחשבת אוכלים בזריקה:
Rashi on Pesachim 60b:1:1.english: Rather, [is it] not during one rite - Even during one rite it is valid, and our Mishnah speaks both of one rite and of two rites. During one rite, such as during the slaughter, it declares it valid, because due to [only] some of those who will eat [it], they do not disqualify [the offering]. And during two rites, such as where he slaughtered [it] for those who can eat it and sprinkled [the blood] for those who cannot eat it, even though the entire sprinkling was for those who cannot eat it — it is valid, because intent regarding those who will eat [the offering] does not [apply] during sprinkling.

Rashi on Pesachim 60b:2:1.hebrew: סיפא בעבודה אחת - רישא אימא לך: אי אף בעבודה אחת, ורבי יוסי היא; אי בשתי עבודות קאמר ולא בעבודה אחת, ור"מ, דאי בעבודה אחת — כשר בלשמו ושלא לשמו, דתפוס לשון ראשון:
Rashi on Pesachim 60b:2:1.english: The latter clause [speaks] of one rite - [As for] the first clause, I can say to you: either [it speaks] even of one rite, and it is [the view of] Rabbi Yose; or it speaks of two rites and not of one rite, and [it is the view of] Rabbi Meir, for if [it were] with one rite, [the offering] would be valid [when performed] for its own sake and not for its own sake, since we hold by the first expression.

Rashi on Pesachim 60b:3:1.hebrew: פסח בשאר ימות השנה - כגון שהפרישו קודם לכן ימים רבים, וקיימא לן דכשר לשלמים בפירקין דלקמן (פסחים ד' ע:). ואם שחטו לפסח, פסול, דלאו זמניה; ואי לשם שלמים שחטו, כשר. והיכא דשחטו לשמו ושלא לשמו, מהו:
Rashi on Pesachim 60b:3:1.english: A Paschal offering on the rest of the days of the year - For example, where one set it aside many days beforehand, and we hold that it is valid as a peace-offering in our chapter below (Pesachim 70b). And if one slaughtered it as a Paschal offering, it is invalid, because it is not its [proper] time; and if one slaughtered it for the sake of a peace-offering, it is valid. And where one slaughtered it [both] for its own sake and not for its own sake, what is [the law]?

Rashi on Pesachim 60b:4:1.english: I stated the teaching - To derive from the rule of binyan av [a general principle] that it is disqualified.

Rashi on Pesachim 60b:4:2.english: Does not remove it from [the status of] not for its own purpose - To adopt the latter expression alone and validate [an offering] slaughtered not for its own purpose and for its own purpose.

Rashi on Pesachim 60b:4:3.english: So too, [intent] not for its own purpose, etc., does not remove it from [the status of] for its own purpose - [That is,] to follow the latter expression and validate it.

Rashi on Pesachim 60b:5:1.hebrew: שכן נוהג - פסולו בכל הזבחים, או לפסול לגמרי בפסח וחטאת, או לפסול מעלות לבעלים לשם חובה בשאר זבחים, כדתנן (זבחים ד' ב.): כל הזבחים שנזבחו שלא לשמן כשרין לזרוק ולהקטיר אימורים ולאכול בשרן, ולא עלו לבעלים לשם חובה, חוץ מפסח וחטאת שפסולין לגמרי. אלמא נוהג בכל הזבחים, הלכך לא אתי לשמו ומפיק לה מידיה לגמרי:
Rashi on Pesachim 60b:5:1.english: For it applies - [That is,] its disqualification [applies] to all sacrifices: either to disqualify [them] completely, in the case of the Paschal offering and the sin-offering, or to disqualify [them] from counting for the owners toward [fulfilling their] obligation, in the case of other sacrifices; as we learned in the Mishnah (Zevachim 2a): "All sacrifices that were slaughtered not for their own sake are valid for sprinkling [the blood], burning the sacrificial portions, and eating their meat, though they do not count for the owners toward [fulfilling their] obligation — except for the Paschal offering and the sin-offering, which are completely disqualified." Thus we see that it applies to all sacrifices; therefore, [intent] for its own sake does not come and remove it completely.

Rashi on Pesachim 60b:5:2.hebrew: תאמר - בפסול דלשמו, שאינו נוהג אלא בפסח בשאר ימות השנה. וכיון דקיל, אתי שלא לשמו ומפיק ליה מידיה:
Rashi on Pesachim 60b:5:2.english: Can you say [so] - regarding the disqualification of [slaughtering] for its own sake, which applies only to the Paschal offering during the other days of the year? And since it is lenient, [intent for] not its own sake comes and removes it from its hand [i.e., overrides it].

Rashi on Pesachim 60b:8:1.hebrew: מהיכא דלא אמר - דאף על גב דהיכא דלא אמר ברישא לשמו ואמר שלא לשמו כשר, היכא דאמר פסול:
Rashi on Pesachim 60b:8:1.english: From [a case] where he did not say [it] - For even though where he did not say "for its own sake" at the beginning and said "not for its own sake" it is valid, where he said [it], it is disqualified.

Rashi on Pesachim 60b:8:2.hebrew: דהא שלא לאוכליו פסול - ואף על גב דסתמיה לאוכליו קאי, אתי שלא לאוכליו ומפיק ליה מסתמיה. וכי אמר ברישא לאוכליו, והדר שלא לאוכליו, לא אתי שלא לאוכליו ומפיק ליה מידי לאוכליו, וכשר:
Rashi on Pesachim 60b:8:2.english: For [when it is slaughtered] for those who cannot eat it, it is disqualified - And even though in its undetermined state it stands [to be offered] for those who can eat it, [the explicit intention] "for those who cannot eat it" comes and removes it from its undetermined state. But when he says first "for those who can eat it" and then "for those who cannot eat it," [the intention] "for those who cannot eat it" does not come and remove it from [its status of] "for those who can eat it," and it is valid.

Rashi on Pesachim 60b:8:3.hebrew: הכי השתא - ומי דמי סתמא דלאוכליו לסתמא דלשמו, דתילפינהו מהדדי? התם, סתמא דלשמו אלים טובא, דכל כמה דלא איעקר ליה שם פסח מיניה, סתמא לשמו קאי, ואפילו הכי כי אמר שלא לשמו, מפיק ליה מסתמיה. הלכך, כי אמר לשמו ברישא נמי, יליף מיניה דאתי שלא לשמו ומפיק ליה מידיה, דלא שאני לן בין היכא דאמר מהיכא דלא אמר. אבל לאוכליו, מי אלים סתמא דידיה דסתמא ליקו להני אוכלין? הא אי בעי, מימשכו הני מיניה ומוכרין אותו לחבורה אחרת:
Rashi on Pesachim 60b:8:3.english: Now, is that so? - And is an unspecified [intention] for those who can eat it similar to an unspecified [intention] for its own purpose, that you would derive them from one another? There, the unspecified [intention] of "for its own purpose" is very strong, for as long as the designation of a Paschal offering has not been uprooted from it, in an unspecified state it stands for its own purpose; and even so, when he says "not for its own purpose," he removes it from its unspecified state. Therefore, when he says "for its own purpose" at the beginning as well, [one] derives from it that "not for its own purpose" comes and removes it from its [status], for there is no difference to us between where he said [it] and where he did not say [it]. However, [with regard to] "for those who can eat it," is its unspecified [intention] so strong that in an unspecified state it stands for these [particular] eaters? Behold, if they wish, these [people] can withdraw from it and sell it to another group.

Tosafot on Pesachim 60b:3:1.hebrew: פסח ששחטו לשמו ושלא לשמו - אומר ר"י דמיבעיא ליה אפי' לר"מ, דסבר בעלמא "תפוס לשון ראשון", דילמא הכא פסול דלשמו — דאינו נוהג בכל הזבחים — לא חשיב למיחל והוי עקירה, או דילמא אפ"ה אמר "תפוס לשון ראשון". אליבא דר' יוסי הוה מצי למיבעי אפילו בשלא לשמו ולשמו, אלא להכי נקט לשמו ושלא לשמו משום דבעיא אפילו אליבא דר"מ:
Tosafot on Pesachim 60b:3:1.english: "A Paschal lamb that one slaughtered for its own purpose and for a different purpose" - R. Yitzchak says that [the Gemara] raises this dilemma even according to R. Meir, who generally holds "grasp the first expression": perhaps here the disqualification of [slaughtering] for its own purpose — which does not apply to all sacrifices — is not significant enough to take effect, and [thus] there is an uprooting [of that intent by the subsequent intent]; or perhaps even so, [R. Meir] says "grasp the first expression." According to R. Yose, [the Gemara] could have raised the dilemma even in [the case of] "for a different purpose and for its own purpose"; rather, this is why it stated "for its own purpose and for a different purpose" — because it raises the dilemma even according to R. Meir.

Tosafot on Pesachim 60b:6:1.hebrew: בשאר ימות השנה - היינו קודם שהגיע זמן הפסח, כדפי' בקונטרס, ולכך בעי עקירה, לפי שעומד לפסח כשיבא, ובכולה שמעתא חשיב ליה דקאי לשמו. אבל לאחר הפסח משמע לקמן (פסחים ד' סד.) דספיקא הוי, דקאמרינן: "ש"מ פסח בשאר ימות השנה בעי עקירה":
Tosafot on Pesachim 60b:6:1.english: On the rest of the days of the year - This means before the time of Pesach has arrived, as Rashi explained, and therefore it requires uprooting [of its designation], because it stands [designated] for Pesach when it arrives; and throughout the entire discussion [the Gemara] considers it as standing for its own purpose. However, after Pesach, it is implied below (Pesachim 64a) that it is a matter of doubt, for we say: "Learn from this [that] a Paschal lamb on the rest of the days of the year requires uprooting."

Tosafot on Pesachim 60b:7:1.hebrew: הכא נמי אתי שלא לשמו ומפיק מידי לשמו - וא"ת: והא לשמו ושלא לשמו כשר לר"מ, ולא אמרינן "אתי שלא לשמו ומפיק מידי לשמו", ושלא לשמו גרידא פסול, אע"ג דסתמא לשמו קאי? ואור"י, דהתם היינו טעמא: דהכשר לשמו נוהג בכל הזבחים, הילכך כי אמר לשמו אלים למיחל טפי, ולא אתי שלא לשמו ומפיק ליה; אבל האי פסול דלשמו אינו נוהג בכל הזבחים, ולהכי לא מקשה ליה אלא מלאוכליו ושלא לאוכליו, דלא שייך אלא בפסח גרידא:
Tosafot on Pesachim 60b:7:1.english: Here too, [the intent] not for its own purpose comes and removes [it] from [the status of] for its own purpose - And if you will say: Isn't [slaughter] for its own purpose and not for its own purpose valid according to Rabbi Meir, and we do not say "[the intent] not for its own purpose comes and removes [it] from [the status of] for its own purpose," whereas [slaughter] not for its own purpose alone is invalid, even though an unspecified [slaughter] stands for its own purpose? And Rabbi Yitzchak says that there, this is the reason: because the validity of [slaughter] for its own purpose applies to all sacrifices; therefore, when he says "for its own purpose," it is stronger to take effect more, and [the intent] not for its own purpose does not come and remove it. However, this invalidation of [slaughter] for its own purpose [on the rest of the days of the year] does not apply to all sacrifices, and therefore [Rav Adda bar Ahava] only objects to him from [the case of] "for those who can eat it and those who cannot eat it," which applies only to the Paschal offering alone.

Tosafot on Pesachim 60b:8:1.hebrew: סתמו להני אוכלין קאי, הני מימשכי כו' - הקשה ריב"א: מה לנו אי לא קאי להני אוכלין? מ"מ סתמא לאוכלין קאי — או להני או לאחריני — דסתמא לא לחולים או לזקנים קאי, ואפ"ה שלא לאוכליו מפיק מלאוכליו; ושלא לאוכליו נמי, אמאי לא עקר לאוכליו דקאמר ברישא? ואומר ר"י: דכששוחט לאוכליו ושלא לאוכליו, אינו כשר אלא על ידי אותם אוכלין ששחט וחישב עליהן, וסתמיה לאו לאלו אוכלין, והרי כאילו לא קאי לאוכליו:
Tosafot on Pesachim 60b:8:1.english: Does it stand in an undetermined state for these eaters? [Perhaps] these will withdraw, etc. - Riva raised a difficulty: What does it matter to us if it does not stand for these [specific] eaters? In any case, in an undetermined state it stands for eaters — either for these or for others — for in an undetermined state it does not stand for the sick or for the elderly. And even so, [intending it] for those who cannot eat it removes it from [its undetermined status of being for] those who can eat it; and [when he slaughters it for those who can eat it and] for those who cannot eat it as well, why does [the latter] not uproot [the intent for] those who can eat it that he stated first? And Ri says: When one slaughters [the offering] for those who can eat it and those who cannot eat it, it is only valid by virtue of those [specific] eaters for whom he slaughtered and had intention; and its undetermined state is not for these [specific] eaters, so it is as if it did not stand for those who can eat it.
